_comment: Unit Roadmap spec. Unit title, phase and section titles come from courses/chemistry/DECISIONS.md; do not add them here. 'measured' must agree with DECISIONS.md 'Assessment shape'. Standards follow reports/chem-ohio-standards-verification.md §5 (CONFIRMED rows as main; inference-only, conditional and VIP-for-a-NONE-section rows as support only); key wording from §4.
big_idea: Everything in this room is matter, and all of it is built from atoms. Students sort matter into **pure substances and mixtures**, follow the experiments that changed the model of the atom, and use an atom's **atomic number and mass number** to count its particles.
builds_on: Middle-school idea of atoms and elements

ican: I can **classify** matter as an element, compound, or mixture, and a mixture as homogeneous or heterogeneous.
I can **tell** physical from chemical change using evidence.
I can **explain** how mixtures are separated physically.
I can **compare** atomic models from Dalton to Rutherford.
I can **explain** what cathode rays and gold foil revealed.
I can **explain** why scientists replace a model when new evidence does not fit it.
I can **find** the protons, neutrons, and electrons in an atom or ion from its symbol and mass number.
I can **explain** what makes two atoms isotopes.
I can **write** an isotope as carbon-14 or as ^{14}C.
I can **explain** why average atomic mass is a weighted average, not a simple one.
I can **calculate** average atomic mass from isotope data.
I can **predict** the most common isotope.

standards_source: Ohio's Learning Standards for Science (adopted 2018) · Chemistry
standards_key: evolution of atomic models/theory; electrons; electron configurations.
SI units, significant figures, dimensional analysis, the mole, molar mass.
types and strengths; effects on melting/boiling point, solubility, vapor pressure.
measured: Daily practice that builds from basic to multi-step problems
Unit test, Day 1: about 25 conceptual multiple-choice questions
Unit test, Day 2: free-response problems, work shown
